rules.licence: A Fish & Game licence has to be carried to fish Lake Wakatipu, and the daily limit is two trout and four salmon.
rules.release: Every fish here goes back: the game keeps a log, not a bag.

zones.name: Lake Wakatipu
zones.advice: Reach two trout and anything you cannot tell from a trout goes back.

rigs.name: Small bright spinner
rigs.hint: Cast out and wound back steadily: what most people fish from the shore here.

rigs.name: Cicada on a floating line
rigs.hint: Laid down close in under the willows on a summer afternoon.

rigs.name: Streamer on a sinking line
rigs.hint: For salmon when they school close to the shore.

species.name: Brown trout
species.note: About seven of every ten fish from the lake are browns. They cruise the edge under the trees, and a careless step sends them out.

species.name: Rainbow trout
species.note: Faster and wilder than a brown: a rainbow runs, turns and comes out of the water.

species.name: Chinook salmon
species.note: Landlocked here, so they stay small. In spring they school close in after small fish; by summer they are down deep.

spots.name: Queenstown Bay beach
spots.note: The town beach, with the Earnslaw's wharf to the west. Trout work along the drop-off early, before the bay gets busy.
spots.source: Otago Fish & Game, Lake Wakatipu (spinning from the shore; the Frankton to Queenstown walkway when time is short)

spots.name: Queenstown Gardens shore
spots.note: The Gardens' side of the bay, under the trees. On a warm afternoon the cicadas that fall from them are what the browns are waiting for.
spots.source: Otago Fish & Game, Lake Wakatipu (cicada patterns along overhanging vegetation in summer)

sources.what: Species, brown trout about 70% of the catch, about 1 kg on average, methods and seasons, shore access
